claims.text: Adding a small, uniform fraction of h-BN nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will produce a self-lubricating composite.
The h-BN composite will reduce friction relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
The h-BN composite will reduce wear relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
A loading of 2–5 wt% h-BN nanoparticles can be introduced into CoCrFeNi with a uniform distribution.
Powder metallurgy or in situ dispersion can be used to incorporate the h-BN nanoparticles into CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will create a homogeneous network of nanoscale h-BN phases embedded in the CoCrFeNi microstructure.
The embedded h-BN phases will provide continuous lubricious interfacial layers.
h-BN has a layered structure with weak interlayer bonding that promotes easy shear.
At low temperatures, the intrinsic lubricity of h-BN will reduce friction in the CoCrFeNi composite.
At high temperatures, h-BN has sufficient thermal stability to maintain a protective lubricious tribofilm.
At high temperatures, h-BN resists oxidation sufficiently to maintain a protective lubricious tribofilm in ambient air.
The lubricating action of h-BN will minimize adhesive wear across the full temperature range.
The lubricating action of h-BN will minimize abrasive wear across the full temperature range.
The anticipated benefits apply under controlled sliding in ambient atmosphere at a fixed load and temperatures no higher than 800 °C.
High-temperature interfacial reactions between h-BN and the metallic phases may alter tribofilm formation.
Nonoptimal h-BN dispersion may change the magnitude of the friction and wear improvements.
A reduction greater than 10% in both coefficient of friction and wear rate at every tested temperature is the proposed success threshold.
